Bug_Details: Math.round(Integer) results in truncation Math.round() called with an integer or long type results in truncation because Math.round only accepts floats or doubles and some integers and longs can’t be represented with float.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by calling Math.round() with integer and long types. Math.round() expects a float or double argument, and when an integer or long is passed, it is implicitly cast to a float or double. For large integers and longs, this casting can lead to loss of precision, resulting in truncation.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the showBug methods with Integer.MAX_VALUE and Long.MAX_VALUE. Since Math.round() casts these values to float and double respectively, precision is lost for these large values, leading to truncation. The test cases expect the original values but receive truncated values, causing the tests to fail.
